reason: NARROWER: 'connecting veins 2 or 3 between adjacent secondaries' are the cross-connecting higher-order veins between secondaries; PO lists cross-vein as a synonym of tertiary leaf vein. Not every flora's connecting vein is strictly third order, hence narrower.

A fragment ('cystoliths present') naming a calcium carbonate concretion inside a cell (a cell inclusion, a substance), not a PO plant structure. Better handled later as presence of cystoliths on the leaf, not as a bearer class.
NARROWER: phyllary is a NARROW synonym of involucral bract (rule C250); 'inner' is a position in the involucral series, and PATO/FLOPO has no 'inner' quality, so the position word is dropped.
NARROWER: the thread-like divisions of a Passiflora-type floral corona (FLOPO_0985020) are its lobes; filiform/capitate are qualities of that lobe.

label: bladder trap
parent: is_a PO_0025001 cardinal organ part; part_of PO_0009025 vascular leaf
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is a small, stalked, hollow, bladder-like suction trap borne on the leaf segments of Utricularia and related Lentibulariaceae, with a trapdoor closing its mouth. NOTE: No class in PO; also the subject of debate on what Utricularia leaves are.
reason: Examples ('bladders dimorphic, stalked', 'lateral', 'ovoid', 1-4 mm) are the Utricularia trap. 'Bladder' is also used for bladder hairs (Chenopodiaceae), so the rule should apply only in Lentibulariaceae. FLOPO-local; PO proposal optional.
Ambiguous: bladder traps, vesicular hairs, inflated fruiting structures ('with dentate foliaceous e...') or cell inclusions in different floras.
EXACT: hyphenated form of the existing FLOPO class label.

target: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) part_of leaf sheath (PO_0020104)
reason: A bamboo culm sheath is the sheath of a culm leaf (leaf sheath of a stem leaf); its apex is the apex region of that sheath (apex pattern: apex part_of the qualified whole).
Location fragment of a count ('vittae 2 on commissure'); the counted part is vitta (FLOPO_0986042), the commissure face is a container, not a bearer. Same treatment as the 'per ...' fragments.

label: aerophore
parent: is_a PO_0025001 cardinal organ part; part_of PO_0009025 vascular leaf
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) of a fern leaf (PO:0009025) that is a pale, often swollen or linear outgrowth or line of aerating tissue at the base of a pinna or on the stipe, serving for gas exchange, as in Thelypteridaceae. NOTE: No aerophore (pneumathode) in PO.
reason: A real fern structure used diagnostically in several fern treatments; no PO class. Worth proposing to PO together with frond/pinna (FLOPO_0985026/0985027).

target: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) of the described part (leaf, leaflet or bract), with presence as quality
reason: A spine at the tip of the described organ (Agave/Bromeliaceae leaves, bracts); 'terminal spine present/absent' is the apex being spine-tipped or not. PO spine leaf (PO_0025173) is a whole leaf turned into a spine, so it does not fit.

label: spadix staminate zone
parent: is_a PO_0009011 plant structure; part_of PO_0030120 spadix inflorescence
definition: A plant structure (PO:0009011) that is the portion of a spadix inflorescence (PO:0030120) bearing the staminate flowers (PO:0025600), as in Araceae. NOTE: Sibling of spadix appendix (FLOPO:0986049); no class for the zones of a spadix in PO.
reason: Shape and length (conic, cylindric, 4 mm long) belong to the zone as a whole, not to each staminate flower, so the part-of-qualified-whole pattern does not fit. Pairs with a pistillate zone class; FLOPO-local, could be proposed to PO with the spadix appendix.
Unclear structure: 'with 2 short stylids at apex' may be style-like appendages of a fruit or the small style lobes of some family; no clear botanical meaning across floras without context.
NARROWER: the lateral lobes of an orchid labellum are labellum lobes; 'lateral' has no position quality (PATO_0001193 is relational) and is dropped.

NARROWER: an ochreola is the small sheath on the flowering stalk of Polygonaceae, formed like an ochrea. Caveat: the FLOPO ochrea class is defined as fused stipules round the stem above a leaf, while an ochreola comes from a bract.
Not a standard term in the glossaries checked; its meaning cannot be fixed from the French fragments ('effilées, 1–3 mm de long').

NARROWER/near exact: PO lists cone scale and ovuliferous scale as synonyms of megasporophyll; a seed cone scale is the ovuliferous scale of a conifer seed cone ('apical sterile' scales are still scales of that cone).
Count fragment ('flowers 1-4 per ocreate fascicle'); a container phrase like the rejected 'per node', 'per axil'.
The tip of the beak is the distal apex of the Carex perigynium; the beak itself has no class and 'beak' alone was rejected as generic, so the apex of the perigynium is the nearest expressible region.

In Proteaceae the pollen presenter is the enlarged distal end of the style, onto which pollen is deposited; its shape and size are those of the style apex region. A dedicated class could follow if more floras use it.
Location fragment of a count ('vittae 1 in each furrow'); counted part is vitta (FLOPO_0986042), the furrow is the container.
NARROWER: knees (Taxodium, mangroves) are knee roots, a RELATED synonym of pneumatophore in PO; 'knees present/absent, grow above water' matches.
Count fragment ('pinnae 20-30 per side of rachis'), as the rejected 'per side'; also a mis-singularised 'rachis'.

NARROWER: pseudostomata of Sphagnum capsules are paired guard-cell-like cells without a functional pore; presence/abundance is read on the nearest PO class. A strict ontologist might prefer a separate class; only bryophyte treatments use it.
NARROWER: the carpocephalum of Marchantiales is the archegoniophore (strictly its head); domed, lobed, umbonate describe the archegoniophore head.

label: pedicel scar
parent: is_a PO_0025001 cardinal organ part; part_of PO_0020122 inflorescence axis
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is the mark left on an inflorescence axis (PO:0020122) where a pedicel (PO:0030112) and its flower or fruit have been shed. NOTE: Modelled on leaf scar (FLOPO:0986052).
reason: A real, diagnostic structure (spacing and prominence of scars on old rachises, e.g. Annonaceae, palms) with no class. Propose to PO together with leaf scar.
NARROWER/exact: same as 'primary lateral vein' and 'lateral nerve' in the previous review (C274, C275); the first lateral veins from the midrib are secondary veins.
Fragment of a ratio or measure ('up to 5 [m / times] height of plant'); height is a quality and the plant is already whole plant, so this is not a part name.
NARROWER: in Carex/Cyperaceae the staminate scale is the bract subtending a staminate flower; the staminate state belongs to the flower it subtends, not the scale.
Ratio fragment ('petals 2.5-3 × as long as calyx'); calyx is the reference part of pattern 10 (ratio to another part), not a new bearer.
